stem.text: Measurements are made to determine the activation energy, $E_\text{a}$, of a reaction.
The diagram shows $E_\text{a}$ on the Boltzmann distribution at temperature $T_1$.

stem.alt: Boltzmann distribution at T1: number of molecules against energy, with the peak at low energy and E_a marked on the falling tail of the curve.

stem.text: Measurements are then made at a higher temperature, $T_2$.
Which diagram correctly shows the Boltzmann distribution and $E_\text{a}$ at $T_2$?

A.alt: Boltzmann curve peaking at about the energy of E_a, with E_a marked just to the right of the peak.

B.alt: Boltzmann curve with its peak to the right of E_a, and E_a marked to the left of the peak.

C.alt: Boltzmann curve with a lower peak at low energy, and E_a marked on the falling tail to the right of the peak.

D.alt: Boltzmann curve with a peak at low energy, and E_a marked just after the peak on the falling tail.
